text.p: Consolidation in the multi-million dollar reinsurance industry will continue as companies strive to become global, a leading industry executive said on Wednesday.
Michael Butt, chief executive of Bermuda-based Mid Ocean Re, made his forecast to an industry conference following an intense period of mergers and acquisitions over the last five months.
"There have been more deals in the reinsurance sector this year than in any of the previous 10 years and they've been driven by the need for global reach," said Butt.
"I see the need for globalisation being a continual driver. There is no doubt this is not a finished play, there are many more acts to come."

The shape of the industry was redrawn over recent months in a wave sparked when General Re took over National Re in the face of rival suiters. Later, Munich Re acquired American Re in the United States, while Swiss Re bought the United Kingdom's largest reinsurer M&G Re.

"In our view to be a series player in the reinsurance market you have to have more than $400 million capital and I believe that the much used phrase 'flight to quality' will continue to be the main force," said Butt.

Reinsurance companies in Bermuda currently fall into three categories -- financial and finite risk reinsurers, excess of loss reinsurers and property casualty reinsurers. However, Butt expects this picture to change.
"In three years these divisions will have blurred and companies will operate in more than one area" he said.

Butt told Reuters it was difficult to predict whether or not there would be more mergers between reinsurers in Bermuda, following the Ace takeover of Tempest Re earlier this year. He said the financial arguments were not compelling, but that situations that present a sound business logic might arise.

"These are challenging times for reinsurance managers. I have no doubts that there will be continued globalisation, continued and I hope enhanced return on equity and some managers will have to learn what shareholder added-value means," said Butt.
